message:
e2e: do not modify the caller's URL in OpenWebSocketForURL

OpenWebSocketForURL rewrote the scheme of the *url.URL it was given:
"https" became "wss", anything else became "ws". Called a second time
with the same URL, the scheme was already "wss", which is not "https",
so it was rewritten to "ws" and the dial spoke plaintext HTTP to the
TLS port. Go's server answers that with "400 Bad Request" before the
request reaches any handler, and the websocket client reports it as
"bad status".

The "Pods should support retrieving logs from the container over
websockets" conformance test builds the URL once and retries the
websocket read with gomega.Eventually. Whenever the first attempt
succeeded but the container had not flushed its output yet, every
retry then failed with "bad status" until the timeout, which is the
signature of the flake in #142284: exactly one hijacked request in the
apiserver log, no further requests, and a final Gomega message noting
that "at one point the function did return successfully" with an
empty string.

Work on a copy of the URL and treat "wss" like "https" so that repeated
calls behave the same as the first. The new unit test dials a TLS test
server three times with the same URL.
